guarantees.claim: Output delta is a purely combinational function of input gamma, defined by the sequence of GF(2^2) operations: a = gamma[3:2] ^ gamma[1:0]; b = aes_mul_gf2p2(gamma[3:2], gamma[1:0]); c = aes_scale_omega2_gf2p2(aes_square_gf2p2(a)); d = aes_square_gf2p2(c ^ b); delta[3:2] = aes_mul_gf2p2(d, gamma[1:0]); delta[1:0] = aes_mul_gf2p2(d, gamma[3:2]).

assumptions.claim: External functions aes_mul_gf2p2, aes_square_gf2p2, and aes_scale_omega2_gf2p2 are pure combinational and correctly compute their advertised GF(2^2) operations (multiplication, squaring, and scaling by omega^2) for all 2-bit inputs.
assumptions.risk: If any sub-function produces incorrect outputs or contains latches/glitches, the computed inverse delta would be wrong, potentially breaking the AES S-box and weakening encryption.

uncertain_points.claim: The correctness of this inverse computation depends entirely on the correctness of the GF(2^2) building blocks (aes_mul_gf2p2, etc.) defined elsewhere; a bug in those functions would propagate to this function.
uncertain_points.cond: must be verified in conjunction with the sub-function implementations
uncertain_points.risk: An error in a sub-function could cause systematic AES S-box failures, breaking the cipher.
